In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SVL is not a suitable tool for this benchmark, because it is not able to achieve the performance of the state of the art.
there are no clear winners or clear losers.
the use of the SVL is not recommendable for the ISPRS 2012 2D semantic labelling benchmark.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained with SVL were not competitive with other approaches, however, it was possible to improve the results by using the conditional random field (CRF) framework.

the use of the height model and NDVI features did not lead to an improved result, the use of the conditional random field approach did not lead to a better result, the use the graph-based segmentation improved the result, and the use of the chessboard segmentation did not lead to any improvement.

the SVL performs very good on the benchmark dataset, but it is not able to compete with state of the art results.
